raw_comment:
1. The line of best fit would represent how young Serena’s opponents got as she got older.
2. I notice that Serena had her most matches between the ages of 14 - 24 and 30 - 36, and her matches decreased in the 24 - 30 year old range of her life.
3. For the two graphs I noticed that two different sets of data were shown, how her world ranking fluctuated over time (when was she top, when was she not), and the bottom graph shows her participation in Grand Slam tournaments and her wins and plays. I wonder about Serena’s world ranking, was she ranked with women all the same ages as her, or was it just general. I also wonder for the Grand Slam graph, are the “plays” times that Serena didn’t win the tournament.
I’d give the top world ranking graph the name: Serena William’s Highs and Lows.
I’d give the Grand Slam graph the name: Grand Tournaments Serena Slammed.

raw_comment:
In the time series graph, it displays Serena Williams’s world ranking in tennis since 1998. It highlights the times when she was No. 1 in the sport in addition to how long she held the spot. It also shows when her ranking dropped. The infographic chart shows Grand Slam tournaments from 1998-2022 and whether or not Serena Williams participated or won. 
 
 
In the time series graph, I notice that the height of Serena Williams’s career was from February 2013 to September 2016 as she remained at the No. 1 world ranking for 186 weeks. Additionally, 2006 and 2017 were her worst years as she lost popularity and her international ranking temporarily. In the infographic chart, I notice that she played in the majority of Grand Slam tournaments that have taken place since 1998. However, she only won 23 while she participated in 80. 
 
I wonder why her popularity fell in 2006 as brought out by the time series graph. I’m also curious as to how she was able to maintain 3 ½ years as the No. 1 spot from 2013-2016. In regards to the infographic chart, I wonder why she failed to play in 20 tournaments. 
 
A headline for graph 1 could be The Popularity of Serena Williams. For graph 2, Grand Slam Games Played by Serena Williams.

raw_comment:
Having analysed the graph, Serena Williams' improvement is clearly displayed by the positive correlation of the scatter plot. As her career progressed, she continued to defeat opponents at every level, including those with up to 10 more years of experience in tennis. 

I wonder what caused to lose to opponents younger than her in the prime of her career. Was she battling mental struggles? Other renowned female athletes such as Liz Cambage, and Simone Biles have also been in the same position. Moreover, if this was the case, what led her to overcome those changes in her mindset?

As an athlete myself, I ask this question to hopefully apply it to my life and learn from one of the best athletes of all time.

Ultimately, this graph demonstrates a positive correlation of Serena Williams' wins (blue data points) as her career advanced asserting herself as the best female tennis player of all time.

raw_comment:
The first graph from the reveal shows her world ranking with the x axis being the year and the y being her rank. The second graph shows the grand slam titles with a color coded legend that shows if she won, played, or did not play the grand slam tournament. 

I notice in the first graph she usually stayed at the top of the ranks, but occasionally fell below. I also noticed how the orange bar represents when she was number one ranked. The second graph shows me she not only played the majority of the grand slam tournaments hosted when she played, but she also won a lot of them.

I wonder how it felt for her to win and be top ranked. Was it exciting or did she have a lot of pressure to stay at the top? 

A headline I would name this would be " One woman, 23 Grand Slam titles "

raw_comment:
Graph 1:
In the first graph "Serena Williams world ranking since 1998", it displays Serena Williams world rankings in the Women's Tennis Association and her rank's changes over her long career. 

I notice that while she is generally at or near the top of the rankings she had several years where she slumped to the middle or fell all the way down to 20th or below.

I wonder what happened in those years where her rank declined that wasn't explained on the graph besides the obvious answer of lacking play that could have impacted her abilities.

A good title for this graph could be "Serena Williams: Consistent Success in Evidence" 

Graph 2: 
The data displayed in the second graph "Williams's Grand Slam Tournaments" is showing that of all the Grand Slam tournaments that Williams was eligible for in that year, which ones did she not play in, play in, or win.

I notice that Serena either played in or won the majority of the Grand Slams she was eligible for each year.

I wonder why Williams didn't play in some of the Grand Slams that she was eligible for and were there and unordinary events that resulted in a win or loss. 

A good alternate title for this graph would be "Serena Williams: A Career Spent At The Finish Line"

raw_comment:
The first graph displays Serena's world ranking and the second graph displays her Grand Slam tournaments.

I noticed that Serena stayed Number 1 in the world ranking for an extremely long time at one point in her career. I also notice that she started winning a lot of the Grand Slam tournaments from 2002 to 2010.

Even though she did peak a lot in her career, I wonder what caused the downward spikes, such as her ranking dropping below 20 in 2006. I also wonder what happened in 2011 where she didn't participate in the Austrailan and French Open and didn't win the Wimbleton and U.S. Open.

One headline that captures the main idea for the first graph could be "You can never get Number 1 once" and for the second graph, "Play for the chance of winning."

raw_comment:
What do you notice?
- The line across the middle of the graph shows which matches Serena Williams won/ lost against other players her own age
- Williams kept a steady ratio of having more wins than losses in across the graph except towards the very end, where more purple begins to appear. 
What do you wonder?
- What began to happen towards the end of the graph that caused her to lose more matches than usual. 
- What caused her be especially dominant from ages 30 to 34. 
What do you think is going on in the graph?
- I think this graph is depicting Serena Williams's wins and losses on a scatter plot. This graph has an x-axis providing her age over the years, and a y-axis providing the ages of her opponents. 
How does this relate to you and your community?
- Going to an all girls school and being surrounded by athletic and powerful young women, this relates to my community and me as it is very inspiring. Serena's mostly successful career from being a younger teenager to 40 years old shows how women can be just as successful in sports as men.

I wonder what kept Serena positively motivated throughout each match, hence she started at a young age and played against more experienced players. 
  
 
This relates to me and my community because shes a vigorous woman that shows and represents determination, girl-power, strength, and motivation. Not only, but she motivated young girls to pursue and have encouragement to play their desired sports such as I, in my community, and  even in other communities!   
 
 
I think a catchy headline for this graph that captivates the graph´s main idea is: The early slaying of Serena Williams significant wins and loses.

raw_comment:
I notice that the vast majority of Serena's games were played while she was older than her opponent. I also notice that she has more wins that losses, and despite that fact she lost both her first and last match ever. Finally, I notice that she only ever had one massively outlier game where she was younger than her opponent by 10+ years despite being 31.

I wonder how Serena kept motivating herself to continue playing even after all her success, lifelong fame and wear and tear on her badge. I wonder how many other players have managed to get to her age range while still playing professionally, and additionally how many managed to maintain their play level while aging like Serena did. 

While she didn't influence me personally, I can see how she impacted the lives of members of my community, the black community. Serena Williams influenced young black people and girls in general to push and work hard for the careers they dreamed of, opened up paths for black people to try for career fields that weren't typically for black people, and pushed black people and women into trying for professional tennis careers that they otherwise wouldn't have even thought about.

A good way to summarize this graphs contents is to say that it is displaying the wins and losses of Serena Williams' career while also comparing the age of both her and her opponent in those matches. A catchy title could be "The Career of the Incredible, Unstoppable, and Undeniably Talented Serena Williams."

raw_comment:
This graph shows the wins and losses throughout Serena Williams's career. It also denotes how old she was and how old her opponent was at the time of the match. Serena Williams, as she aged, became the older opponent in the majority of her matches. As she grew older, however, she did not decrease in playing level. In her early 30s, Williams played the most amount of the matches and also appears to have won the majority. She seems to have a higher winning streak against younger opponents but has a high concentration of losses against players her age. This is likely because opponents had the same level of skill and the same amount of experience. The graph begs the question, as Williams aged, were her physical capabilities limited or did her experience propel her to be a better player?
At certain points in the graph, there are gaps in data. Around age 22, it seems as though no matches were played. Certain points also show a trend of losses. After her mid-30s, Williams played fewer matches and the amount of wins and losses appears to be split evenly. 
I would headline the graph, "Serena Williams Proves: Age is just a Number".

I notice that there are far more blue dots then purple, meaning shes won more matches then shes lost.  I also noticed that shes always played and beat people around the same age bracket, always about 10 or so years older, or younger then her. 

I wonder what went through her mind after every match, win or loss. I also wonder how many different parts of the world all of these matches were played in. 

This relates to me because I used to play tennis and when I did, I played for many reasons, but one being I wanted to be like Williams sisters, specifically Serena. 

This graph shows Serena Williams's professional career's wins and losses. A good headline could be " Serena Williams, A tennis icon "

From my class:

We notice that at the beginning, her championship matches were a year apart and then they became more frequent.  There were more championship matches when she was 30-35yo and less from 35-40yo.  We wonder what was her overall win/loss record?  Who were her first and last opponents?  What happened when she was 29 and 36 (no data)?  Are there more older athletes still performing at a high level today (i.e. Tom Brady, LeBron James), or are they more celebrated now?  For impact, we wonder how engineers are adapting.  Do they need to design products differently with older athletes in mind?  We also talked about recovery processes.  Do we have better recovery processes and procedures already available to extend the life of the athlete, or is this something we need to continue developing?  Our headline:  "No matter the age, Serena is best."

raw_comment:
What a response on the Serena graph! Your responses came from across the country and several countries, with the most from Mexico. Thanks to the over 600 students who responded.

Two schools had a slew of great headlines, so we’d like to give a shout out to many of them. From Perth Amboy High School in New Jersey, shout outs for “Serena Williams Serves Greatness Despite Age Gap” by Ashley, “Serena's Domination: Age Is Just a Number” by Samuel, “Never Letting Age Stop Her, Serena Williams's Track Record" by Sebastian and "Serena Williams SLAMS Through Competition Despite Age" by Noah.  From Andover, Massachusetts, shout outs for “Serena Williams: Dominant No Matter The Age” by May and “Age Was No Barrier: Serena’s Success Story” by Wyatt. And, finally, “Serena Willams still catching dubs at the age of 40” by Isaac from Great Neck North.

You can continue to post responses. Please check back by Friday, Sept.16 to see the Reveal with the free link to the original New York Times article plus a link to more Serena graphs, some questions about the graph, and a few Stat Nuggets.

Signing off – Sharon Hessney of Boston, who was astounded by Serena’s power, concentration and style in last week’s U.S. Open, and Corey Andreasen of The Hague Netherlands, who is amazed by the number of barriers Serena has smashed, as well as the number of opponents of all ages.

raw_comment:
This graph depicts Serena's wins and losses in relation to her age and her opponent's age. The blue dots represent her wins, and the purple dots represent her losses; the majority of her matches resulted in a win, of course, hence the overwhelming amount of blue dots. For most of her tennis career, she was older than her opponents. I would say that the average age of a pro tennis player was around 20-24 years old. At 25 years of age, Serena started becoming the older opponent. Clearly the graph proves that age does not affect Serena’s chances of winning and her play, nor did it affect the length of her tennis career. 

I wonder why there were no recorded matches when Serena was 29 and 36? What stopped her from playing? An injury? A personal issue?

raw_comment:
This graph depicts Serena's wins and losses in relation to her age and her opponent's age. The blue dots represent her wins, and the purple dots represent her losses; the majority of her matches resulted in a win, of course, hence the overwhelming amount of blue dots. For most of her tennis career, she was older than her opponents. I would say that the average age of a pro tennis player was around 20-24 years old. At 25 years of age, Serena started becoming the older opponent. Clearly the graph proves that age does not affect Serena’s chances of winning and her play, nor did it affect the length of her tennis career. 

I wonder why there were no recorded matches when Serena was 29 and 36? What stopped her from playing? An injury? A personal issue?

raw_comment:
Graph name: Serena’s Badassery.
As a group, there was a lot we noticed and wondered about after looking at the graph. She took a break between ages 28-30 and 35-37. There are more wins than losses. She played more games when she was younger. After her pregnancy, she made a comeback in her thirties and played a lot. She played the most games between the ages of 29-35. I wonder why she took a break from playing at ages 35-37. She beat many older/more experienced players as a young player. The losses are really spread out, there isn’t one cluster or one year/age that she was notably worse. This shows us that age is not that important of a factor in performance. This topic impacts the world because it teaches young women that it all starts somewhere. Serena began at 14 years old, it is never too early to start your passions.

This graph demonstrates the wins and losses over the course of Professional Tennis player Serena Williams's career. However, there are small breaks in her career, for example between 28 and 30 as well as at 36.

Serena Williams's overall performance relates to me and my community because of how much of an inspiration she is to athletes and women all over the world. She proved that while she is a woman in sports, she proved to be worthy and important in the sports world.

This graph shows Serena Williams's career wins and losses as she has aged as well as her opponents.

Williams lost her first and second game

Welcome to Wednesday's live moderation of “What’s Going On in This Graph?”  

Today’s graph compares the ages of Serena Williams and her opponents for all of her championship tennis matches over her 27-year career.

From 9 am – 2 pm E.T. today, share with us your responses online to these three questions -- "What do you notice?”, “What do you wonder?"  and “How will this affect you?”  Plus, please share with us a catchy headline that captures the ideas in these graphs. We look forward to replying to your discoveries.

By Friday morning, we’ll reveal the online article that included this graph plus other Serena graphs.  

Note that you can get a link to your response (and replies made to it) to share with your teacher and classmates by clicking the response box below your response “Email me when my comment is published.”  

Please visit our archive to see all graphs in this series (tinyurl.com/NYTGraphs).
View our archives that link to all past releases, organized by topic (tinyurl.com/NYTGraphsTopicIndex), 
graph type (tinyurl.com/NYTGraphsTypeIndex) and 
Stat Nugget (tinyurl.com/NYTGraphsStatNuggetsIndex).  

The next “What’s Going On In This Graph?” will be released by Friday, September 16 with moderation on Wednesday, September 21.  The topic – Tree Rings & Climate.  Keep noticing and wondering.

1. What do you notice?
I notice how many matches Serena Williams won depending on her age, and the age of her opponents. Her losses were fairly consistent across all her time playing tennis, but she definitely wins more matches than loses. It seems like she pretty consistently plays against people that are the same age (meaning the age of her opponents doesn’t change, not that she is the same age as them all the time). Ever since she turned 28, she very rarely plays people older than her.

2. What do you wonder?
Did she take a break from playing tennis around ages 35-36? There’s a large gap in data in that year. There is also no data when she was 22 years old and somewhere around 29 years old as well. 

3. What impact does this have on you and your community?
This doesn’t have a very large impact on me or my community. My school does have a tennis team, so some of my classmates might look up to her and be sad that she's done playing tennis, but other than that there isn’t a huge impact.

raw_comment:
What do you notice?

I noticed that as she got more older, she would beat opponents that were older than her. When she was 14 she had her first lost but she didn't let that stop her from playing. 

What do you wonder? 

I wonder what inspired her to begin playing tennis. Also, what do the gaps mean in between 28 and 30. What goes on in her opponents mind while competing against her?

How does this relate to you and your community?

In regards of me, I'm not much of a tennis player because it doesn't catch my attention but in regard of my community, most of the students in my school play sports and having such an inspiring role model such as Serena Williams makes other be motivated to over achieve and at the end, all hard work will pay off for you.

What's going on in the graph?

In the graph, you can see Serena's win and loss record from when she began up until the present. 
Headline: 
Serena Williams, Queen of the Court.
